beats.narration_text: Hi — I'm Sudhanva, with this week's STEM explainer for the RL Environments project: target networks, and what our logs show when one moves too often.

props.command: Our QMIX value estimate ran away. Pull the prediction and target logs and show me what the target network was doing.
output: grid, default sync: team value estimate 40 at 150k steps · team food 0.00
free world, seed 2: prediction 48 → 865,716 by 500k · target within 3.4%
sync every 2,000 updates: largest prediction 1.2–10.5 across 11 runs

beats.narration_text: Q-learning trains toward its own next guess. If that guess moves every time the network learns, the network chases itself. So the guess comes from a frozen copy that only updates now and then.

props.text:
Q-learning trains toward
the right answer
so hold that guess still

beats.narration_text: Here's the target in our code. The online network picks the next move; the frozen copy scores it. The team reward plus ninety-nine percent of that score is what the prediction is pulled toward.

shot.new_visual_element: Verbatim value_based.py lines (double Q: a_star from self.q, scored by q_next_target; target = team + gamma · not_done · mixer_target(...)) beside the typeset target y = r_team + γ(1 − d)·Q_tot,copy(s′, a′) with a′ chosen by the online network; γ = 0.99 from ValueConfig

full target y = r_team + 0.99 (1 − d) Q_tot,copy(s′, a′) writes on; arrow from y to the prediction

beats.narration_text: Every five hundred updates, the code overwrites the copy with the live network's weights. Between syncs the copy holds still, so the prediction has a fixed thing to catch up to.

shot.new_visual_element: Verbatim sync lines (updates % target_update == 0 → q_target.load_state_dict(q.state_dict()), mixer_target likewise); a constructed timeline: the live weights drift every update while the copy is a staircase that jumps only at syncs; labels from the config: every 500 updates = 1,000 env steps, 998 syncs per 1M-step run

beats.narration_text: Here's prediction and target climbing together in our logs. In one free-world run, prediction and target climbed together, from forty-eight to over eight hundred thousand by five hundred thousand steps, never more than a few percent apart.

beats.narration_text: In test runs that synced every two thousand updates, the prediction never passed about ten. Paired with half the learning rate, QMIX on the grid went from zero point one three to eight point four four.
